pages.lesson:
LESSON: PATTERN WRITING

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.5: Pattern Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Pattern Writing. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns in class.
2. Hold writing tools appropriately when writing patterns.
3. Enjoy participating in pattern writing activities in class. using ICT devices such as using the writing wizard and ZEBRA applications. sand trays or slate boards as the teacher demonstrates.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns in class.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use ICT devices to make simple line patterns in class. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Hold writing tools appropriately when writing patterns.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to hold writing tools appropriately when writing patterns. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Enjoy participating in pattern writing activities in class. using ICT devices such as using the writing wizard and ZEBRA applications. sand trays or slate boards as the teacher demonstrates.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy participating in pattern writing activities in class. using ICT devices such as using the writing wizard and ZEBRA applications. sand trays or slate boards as the teacher demonstrates. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Pattern Writing.
2. Explain Pattern Writing to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Pattern Writing.
4. Show that you can: Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns in class.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Pattern Writing. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Pattern Writing important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns in class.
2. Hold writing tools appropriately when writing patterns.
3. Enjoy participating in pattern writing activities in class. using ICT devices such as using the writing wizard and ZEBRA applications. sand trays or slate boards as the teacher demonstrates.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
